info.name: ZoikoTax API (v1)
info.description:
**Generated from `contracts/openapi/ztax.v1.yaml` — do not edit.**

Run `npm run postman` in `contracts/` after changing the contract or the overlay. A hand edit fails CI (ADR-0010 §2.1): a hand-maintained collection is a second, kinder statement of what the API is.

Contract digest: `sha256:9d29a04512947c4b4a47e89a21a9ccebca2683f70f6d0c629965f6b2e915b7ba`

Import and run; there is no environment to select. `baseUrl` defaults to the local cell and every other value rides along as a collection variable.

## Before you run it

Bring the stack up (`docker compose up --build`), which bootstraps the `acme` tenant and its administrator. Then run the whole collection: `02 · Sign in` opens the session everything below depends on.

Folder `90` is the one worth reading. Each request there sends something a well-behaved client would never send, and each asserts a control from the ADRs against an endpoint that exists today.

Folders `06` and `07` exercise the determination surface and are skipped unless `runDetermination` is `true`: they need a cell with a content bundle and a session holding `OPERATOR`, which the local stack's bootstrap administrator does not have. Paths still to be built are listed in `pendingPaths`, so a 404 there reports as *not implemented yet* rather than as a wall of red.

item.name: 00 · Health — served, and deliberately not in the contract
item.description:
An orchestrator calls these; no SDK does. They carry no session, their bodies are plain text, and declaring them in the contract would generate client methods nobody should call and make a liveness probe a compatibility commitment (ADR-0010 §2.6).

They are added by the generator rather than derived from the contract, and `contract_test.go` keeps the same exception register on the server side.

request.description: Liveness: the process is running and can serve. It touches no dependency on purpose — a liveness probe that failed when the database was down would get the process killed, which does not fix a database and does lose the in-memory content bundle.

request.description: Readiness: this replica can take traffic right now. Unlike liveness it does check the cell store, because a replica that cannot reach it should leave the rotation rather than serve one 503 per caller.

request.description:
Report this deployment's effective capability

Effective capability, not entitlement: the intersection of content
state, security, QA and commercial entitlement (ADR-0010 §2.6).

Unauthenticated, because a client needs to know whether a cell can serve

problem should not need a credential to report which cell and which
content bundle it reached.

`content` is absent in a cell with no bundle loaded, which is a
legitimate deployment before A4. Absent rather than null: "no content"
and "content with no identity" are different facts (ADR-0011 P3).

item.name: 02 · Sign in
item.description: Opens the session every folder below depends on. The response carries no token — the session is an `HttpOnly` cookie Postman's cookie jar keeps for you.

item.name: POST /v1/auth/sign-in — Open a session

request.description:
Open a session

Exchanges a tenant slug, an email address and a password for an opaque
session cookie.

The response carries **no token**. The session identifier is in a
`__Host-`-prefixed, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie that JavaScript
cannot read, which is why the browser client has nothing to store and
nothing to leak (ADR-0019 C8, ADR-0020).

A failure does not distinguish an unknown subject from a wrong password.
The difference is an account-enumeration oracle and a caller can do
nothing with it, so both are `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`.

// one cannot be revoked. The absence of it here is the design.
pm.test('the session cookie is set HttpOnly', function () {

item.name: 05 · Contract conformance — with a session
item.description:
Requests a well-behaved client would never send, to endpoints that need a session. Each asserts a control, and each runs against an endpoint that exists today — so a green row here is evidence rather than an aspiration.

They sit before `08 · Sign out` because they need the session it ends; after it they could only return 401, which is evidence of nothing but the run order.

item.name: Unknown field is rejected, not ignored

request.description:
ADR-0011 §2.1 P5 at the transport boundary.

Silently dropping an undeclared field would let two different requests digest identically, which is exactly the property an idempotency record depends on (ADR-0013 §2.4). It is also the common shape of a real integration bug: a client sends `displayname` where the contract says `displayName`, and a server that ignores it creates a user with no display name and reports success.

exec: pm.test('a field the contract does not declare is rejected', function () {

item.name: Explicit null is rejected

request.description:
ADR-0011 §2.1 P3.

"Explicitly cleared" and "not supplied" are different facts with different consequences, and a canonical form that collapses them erases the difference from the evidence too. So `null` is an error rather than something to normalise.

item.name: 06 · Determination — needs content and an OPERATOR
item.description:
Quote, commit, read and replay one line against the cell's active pack. `commitTransaction` captures the decision into `decisionId`, and the replay after it must say `MATCH` — the W2 exit gate in four requests. `adjustTransaction` then corrects that decision under the bundle that made it (ZTAX-DET-REQ-0030).

Skipped unless `runDetermination` is `"true"`, because it needs two things the local stack does not give the bootstrap administrator: a content bundle (`ZTAX_CONTENT_DIR`, see `make content`) and the `OPERATOR` role. The request bodies are the worked pack's inputs.

item.name: POST /v1/quotes — Quote a transaction without recording it

request.description:
Quote a transaction without recording it

`OPERATOR` or `ANALYST`. Evaluates the input against the cell's active
content bundle by exactly the path a commit takes, then discards it:
no decision, no evidence, no idempotency record.

**A quote is an estimate; only a commit is a decision** (ADR-0004
§2.7). Every quote is `authoritative: false`, whatever the
deployment's authorization level, and must not be filed or invoiced
from.

The input is named the way content reads it. Which values a line
carries, and what they are called, is decided by the active pack, not
by this contract — the worked pack reads `line.netAmount`,
`line.quantity` and two flags, and a read set holding
`threshold.ecoLevyYtd`. A value the pack reads and the request omits is
a `400`; so is an accumulator the pack does not read.

response.name: 200 · VAT and the eco levy, advisory

item.name: POST /v1/transactions:commit — Commit a transaction and record its decision

header.description:
A key the client mints before the first attempt and reuses, unchanged,
on every retry of the same request (ADR-0013). Opaque to the server: it
is compared, never parsed. Scoped to the tenant and to this endpoint, so
a key used for a commit can never match an adjust.

request.description:
Commit a transaction and record its decision

`OPERATOR` only. Evaluates the input against the active content bundle
and records the result as an immutable decision, with the two evidence
objects that let it replay exactly (ADR-0011 §2.8).

**`Idempotency-Key` is mandatory** (ADR-0013 §2.1). A retry with the
same key and the same body returns the original response verbatim,
with `Idempotent-Replay: true`, and records nothing new. The same key
with a different body is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE`; a key whose first
request is still running is `409 REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS` with
`Retry-After`. Neither executes. Bodies are compared in canonical form,
so member order and whitespace do not matter and a decimal's scale
does — `"45.00"` and `"45.0"` are different requests.

A validation failure is recorded against the key and replayed on
retry, because the same request fails the same way. A transient
failure (`503`) is not: the key is released and a retry is a genuine
new attempt.

`supersedes` corrects an earlier decision for the same `businessKey`.
It must name the current version; a decision is never edited, and a
correction is a new decision linked to the old (ADR-0003).

Before A4 every decision is `ADVISORY` and `authoritative: false`.

exec: pm.test('commitTransaction returns a status the contract declares', function () {
pm.test('the decision is recorded, and advisory before A4', function () {

item.name: GET /v1/decisions/{decisionId} — Read a recorded decision

request.description:
Read a recorded decision

`OPERATOR`, `ANALYST` or `AUDITOR`. What the decision emitted is read
from its result evidence and verified against the digest the decision
names, so a response is never built from a record that has come apart
from its evidence — that is a `500 EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY` instead.

exec: pm.test('getDecision returns a status the contract declares', function () {

item.name: POST /v1/replay/{decisionId} — Replay a recorded decision and compare it byte for byte

request.description:
Replay a recorded decision and compare it byte for byte

`OPERATOR`, `ANALYST` or `AUDITOR`. Rebuilds the decision's result from
its envelope alone, against the content bundle the envelope names —
never the one active now — and compares the canonical bytes with the
result that was recorded (ADR-0003 §3.3, ADR-0011 §2.8).

The verdict is data, not an error. `DIVERGED` names the first path at
which the two results differ; `BUNDLE_UNAVAILABLE` means this cell no
longer holds the bundle the decision was made under, which is a fact
about the cell rather than about the decision. Evidence that no longer
matches its digest, or a record that disagrees with its envelope, is a
`500 EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY` instead: that is an incident, not a verdict.

Nothing is recorded. Replaying twice gives the same answer.

response.name: 200 · The runtime no longer reproduces the recorded result

exec: pm.test('replayDecision returns a status the contract declares', function () {
pm.test('ADR-0011 §2.8 — the decision just committed replays exactly', function () {

item.name: POST /v1/transactions:adjust — Correct a recorded decision under the content that made it

header.description:
A key the client mints before the first attempt and reuses, unchanged,
on every retry of the same request (ADR-0013). Opaque to the server: it
is compared, never parsed. Scoped to the tenant and to this endpoint, so
a key used for a commit can never match an adjust.

request.description:
Correct a recorded decision under the content that made it

`OPERATOR` only. Records a CORRECTION of an earlier decision
(ZTAX-DET-001 §10.4) as a new decision superseding it. `supersedes` is
required and must name the current version for the `businessKey`.

The correction is evaluated against the content bundle that made the
decision it supersedes — the bundle its replay envelope names — and
never against the active one (ZTAX-DET-REQ-0030). A credit issued
today against an invoice from an earlier content release corrects tax
charged under that release's rates and rules. If that bundle is not
loaded in the cell, the request is refused with
`503 NO_CONTENT_BUNDLE` and nothing is recorded; it is never quietly
re-evaluated under current content.

Idempotency works as on `:commit`, with its own key scope: the same
`Idempotency-Key` value on `:commit` and `:adjust` names two different
keys (ADR-0013 §2.2).

Before A4 every decision is `ADVISORY` and `authoritative: false`.

response.name: 201 · An advisory correction, made under the original bundle

item.name: 07 · Determination conformance — needs content and an OPERATOR
item.description:
The ADR-0013 and ADR-0011 controls on `POST /v1/transactions:commit`, each asserted against the running endpoint.

Requests 1 to 4 share one idempotency key, minted once per run into `reusedKey`, so a second run against the same cell exercises the same four outcomes rather than replaying the first run's.

Skipped unless `runDetermination` is `"true"`, for the reason `06` gives.

item.name: Idempotency · 1 · first commit with a fixed key

request.description: ADR-0013 §2.4. The first of four: this one establishes the record, and requests 2 to 4 are the interesting ones.

item.name: Idempotency · 2 · same key, same body

request.description: Must return the *original* response, byte for byte, and record nothing. A retry that produced a second decision would be a second fiscal record for one transaction, which is the Critical risk in Build Plan §8.

exec: pm.test('the retry is the original response, verbatim', function () {

item.name: Idempotency · 3 · same key, DIFFERENT body

request.description:
Must be a 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSE` and must not execute (ADR-0013 §2.4).

Replaying the original response would be worse than either alternative: the caller would believe the amount it sent was the amount recorded.

exec: pm.test('a reused key is refused, not replayed', function () {

item.name: Idempotency · 4 · same key, same value at a different scale

request.description:
`"45.0"` is not `"45.00"`. Scale is semantic (ADR-0011 §2.2), so the canonical request digest differs and this is a different request under a used key.

A server that compared parsed numbers would replay request 1 here, and hand back a decision made at a precision the caller did not send.

exec: pm.test('scale is part of the request', function () {

item.name: Idempotency · 5 · no key at all

request.description: `Idempotency-Key` is mandatory on `:commit`, `:adjust`, `:refund` and `POST /v1/batches` (ADR-0013 §2.1). Rejected before any work begins.

exec: pm.test('a keyless commit is refused', function () {

item.name: Canonical form · a fiscal amount sent as a JSON number

request.description:
**The request in this collection that matters most.**

`"amount": 45.0` must be rejected, never coerced. A 2xx here is a Critical finding rather than a test failure: RFC 8785 serializes JSON numbers through IEEE 754 doubles (ADR-0011 §1.1), so an amount that is ever a JSON number has lost precision before canonicalization sees it — and the loss is invisible, because 45.0 survives and 0.1 does not.

The body is raw text rather than a structured one, because the whole point is to send a token a correct client cannot produce.

exec: pm.test('a JSON number is never an amount', function () {

request.description: ADR-0011 §2.1 P3 on the path where it costs the most. "The amount was explicitly cleared" and "the integration did not send an amount" are different events with different fiscal consequences.

exec: pm.test('null is refused rather than normalised', function () {
